title: 脚光浴びる実力派の建設株
extracted_text:
六甲山系の麓に位置する神戸市・一里山地区。かつて阪神大震災に見舞われたこの地で、安全強化のための土砂災害対策工事が完成しつつある。マンションや老人ホームが立ち並ぶ高台の急斜面に格子状に張り巡らせた鉄製のケーブルだ。工事を手掛けるのは ライト工業 （1926）。3月の引き渡しへ最終点検の作業が進んでいる。

「現地の斜面は起伏が大きく、一般的な補強手法であるコンクリート吹きつけでは手間や人手がかかる」（一里山工区の三浦克作業所長）。ライト工業の独自技術「ESネット工法」は、鉄筋のロックボルトを地中3.5メートルの深さまで等間隔に打ち込み、地表面でワイヤケーブルを格子状に連結して交点のプレートで押さえつける。斜面の形状によらず柔軟に敷設できる手法だ。

網の目状なので樹木を残せるうえ、耐久性が高い素材を使うため完成後の保守が基本的に不要な強みもある。「経済性と施工性の高さを両立した工法だ」（三浦氏）。この現場の工期はおよそ7カ月。約2400平方メートルの急斜面に600本超のボルトを打ち込み、本体工事の人員は6人ほどとコンクリート工法のほぼ半数で済んだという。

ライト工業の株価は2026年2月下旬にかけて断続的に上場来高値を更新した。騰勢を強めたのはこの1年ほどで、24年末比でほぼ2倍になった。1943年にトンネルの防水工事で創業し、地盤改良や斜面・のり面工事といった特殊土木に事業領域を広げてきた。経営戦略の中軸に据える防災・減災分野の重要性と施工技術に光が当たった。

阿久津和浩社長は「災害対策のインフラ需要は強まるばかり。技術力を武器に業界をリードしたい」と話す。液状化対策や耐震補強で欠かせない地盤改良も伸びている。最新の「コンダクションナビ工法」は地上の構造物を避けて斜め方向から高精度削孔するため、日常のインフラ運用を妨げずに工事でき、羽田空港や福岡空港といった主要インフラで採用実績を重ねる。

日本は防災対策だけでなくインフラの老朽化にも直面している。

25年には埼玉県八潮市で、下水道管の腐食による大規模な道路陥没事故が起きた。建設経済研究所（東京・港）の中原壮一朗研究員は「同様の事故は全国各地で頻発する可能性がある。インフラを維持、修繕するニーズは非常に強まっている」と指摘する。

石破茂政権（当時）は25年6月、向こう5年間で防災・減災のインフラ強化に20兆円強を投じる「第1次国土強靭化実施中期計画」を閣議決定。政権を引き継いだ高市首相も「令和の国土強靭化対策」を掲げ、株式市場でも技術と実績があるインフラの担い手に注目が集まった。

水関連インフラで膨らむ更新需要に大忙しの1社が 月島ホールディングス （6332）だ。上下水道プラントなどの設計・建設を手がけ、浄水場や下水処理場の汚泥処理分野のシェアは国内トップ級を誇る。26年3月期は売上高が前期比3%増の1440億円、純利益は政策保有株式の売却益も重なり2.2倍の150億円とともに過去最高を見込む。

月島HDは「国内の水道管だけでも総延長で地球18周分ぐらいの長さがあり、時間をかけて更新されていく」とみている。水インフラは集中的に投資された1990年代後半から更新サイクルを迎え、老朽化対応の引き合いが強まっている。連結受注残高は25年末時点で3317億円と年間売上高の2倍強に積み上がった。

現在はJFEグループと水道用鋼管事業の統合に向け協議を進めており、効率的に稼ぐ体制強化を進めている。

（篠崎健太、阿部真也、安田亜紀代、佐藤梨紗が担当した。グラフィックスは久保庭華子）

［デジタル版・日経ヴェリタス2026年2月28日号トップストーリーを一部要約］
translated_text:
Kobe City's Ichiriyama district, located at the foot of the Rokko Mountains. In this area, which was devastated by the Great Hanshin Earthquake, construction work to reinforce slopes against sediment disasters is nearing completion. This involves a grid-like network of steel cables installed on the steep hillside where apartments and nursing homes stand. The work is being carried out by Light Industry (1926). Final inspection is underway ahead of the March handover.

"The local slopes have significant irregularities, making conventional reinforcement methods like concrete spraying quite labor-intensive," says Kai Miura, supervisor of the Ichiriyama work zone. Light Industry's proprietary "ES Net Method" involves driving reinforced rock bolts into the ground at equal intervals to a depth of 3.5 meters, connecting wire cables in a grid pattern on the surface, and securing the intersections with plates. This method can be installed flexibly regardless of the slope's shape.

Because it's mesh-like, trees can be preserved, and the use of durable materials means post-completion maintenance is essentially unnecessary. "This method achieves both high economic efficiency and constructability," says Miura. The project took about seven months. Over 600 bolts were driven into a steep slope of approximately 2,400 square meters, with only about 6 workers needed for the main work—roughly half the workforce required for concrete methods.

Light Industry's stock price intermittently hit record highs through late February 2026. The upward momentum has built over the past year, nearly doubling from the end of 2024. Founded in 1943 with tunnel waterproofing work, the company expanded its business into special civil engineering, including ground improvement and slope/facing work. The importance of disaster prevention and mitigation—an central pillar of its business strategy—and its construction expertise are gaining attention.

President Kazuhiro Akutsu says, "Demand for disaster prevention infrastructure continues to grow. We aim to lead the industry using our technical strength." Ground improvement work, essential for liquefaction countermeasures and seismic reinforcement, is also expanding. The latest "Conduction Navi Method" enables high-precision oblique drilling while avoiding above-ground structures, allowing construction without disrupting daily infrastructure operations. It's been adopted at major infrastructure facilities like Haneda and Fukuoka airports.

Japan faces not only disaster preparedness challenges but also aging infrastructure.

In 2025, a large road collapse occurred in Yashio City, Saitama Prefecture, caused by corroded sewage pipes. Researcher Soichiro Nakahara at the Construction Economics Institute (Minato-ku, Tokyo) notes, "Similar accidents could occur frequently across various regions. Demand for infrastructure maintenance and repair is very strong."

The Ishiba cabinet (at the time) decided in June 2025, through a cabinet meeting, to invest over 20 trillion yen in disaster prevention and mitigation infrastructure reinforcement over the next five years—the first National Resilience Implementation Medium-Term Plan. The administration succeeded by Prime Minister Takaichi has also promoted "Reiwa National Resilience Measures," and the stock market is focusing on infrastructure players with technology and track records.

One company busy with growing replacement demand in water-related infrastructure is Tsukishima Holdings (6332). Engaged in designing and constructing water and wastewater treatment plants, it boasts a top-share in domestic sludge treatment at water purification and wastewater treatment facilities. For the fiscal year ending March 2026, it forecasts sales of 144 billion yen, up 3% from the previous year, and net profit of 15 billion yen, including gains from policy-holding stock sales—2.2 times higher—both representing record highs.

Tsukishima HD observes, "In Japan alone, water pipes total a length equivalent to about 18 times the Earth's circumference, and they are being replaced gradually." Water infrastructure invested intensively in the late 1990s is now entering its replacement cycle, and inquiries for aging-related responses are increasing. Its consolidated order backlog at the end of 2025 reached 331.7 billion yen, more than double annual sales.

Currently, it's in discussions with the JFE Group to integrate its water pipe business, strengthening its efficient earnings structure.

(Kenta Shinozaki, Shinichi Abe, Akiko Yasuda, and Risa Sato contributed. Graphics by Hanako Kuboniwa)

[Summary of a top story from the digital edition of Nikkei Veritas, February 28, 2026]
